title: Thread-Safe Lazy Attribute Descriptor
instructions: Implement the `lazy` descriptor in `lazy.py`: a thread-safe, non-data descriptor that computes a method once per instance and caches it in `obj.__dict__`. Use double-checked locking, never cache exceptions, cache a legitimate `None`, return the descriptor on class access, and fail loudly in `__set_name__` if one `lazy` object is bound to two names.

evidence.label: Computes once and stores the value in the instance __dict__
Class access returns the descriptor, which records its attribute name
del invalidates the cache and plain assignment overrides it (non-data descriptor)
An exception is not cached, so the next access recomputes
Eight simultaneous readers trigger exactly one computation
Binding one lazy to two names raises TypeError mentioning 'two names'
A None result is cached rather than treated as a miss
Different lazy attributes cache independently and work through inheritance
